title: When AI makes execution cheap, verification becomes the scarce resource that reprices trust
content:
a16z crypto's core economic claim: when execution becomes cheap through AI, **verification becomes the scarce resource**. Blockchains, onchain attestations, and decentralized identity systems shift the economic boundary of safe agent deployment by providing clear, auditable history instead of treating AI as a black box.

**Why it matters:** the bottleneck in agent adoption is not capability but the counterparty question — *can this agent be trusted with money and authority?* Systems that make agent behavior verifiable capture the value that trust intermediaries capture today.

**Converging claim:** Microsoft researchers independently frame the agentic economy as one where "trust, not attention, is the scarce resource."

Source: a16z crypto, "5 Ways Blockchains Can Help AI Agents" (https://a16zcrypto.com/posts/article/5-ways-blockchains-help-ai-agents/).
description: Auditable onchain history replaces black-box faith: attestations and decentralized identity shift the boundary of where agents can be safely deployed.
